criteria.demand: Reads pace the sender through explicit bounded demand; no drain case exists in the caller contract.
criteria.event: The producer delivers drain as one more session event item beside text, binary and close.
criteria.mixed: Bounded demand paces file and process sources while sockets keep an explicit drain event.

drain.instructions: How should W3-style drain and backpressure reach the caller?

criteria.later: Ship the pull core first and add consume only when maintained programs prove the close boilerplate is a real burden.
criteria.now: Ship pull plus a consume helper together so callers can choose either form from the start.
criteria.pilot: Ship pull plus one consume adapter over it for a single domain now, and generalize only on evidence.

sugar.instructions: If pull is the core, when should an L-style consume helper be built?

criteria.domain: Build per-domain drive operations with per-domain decision nominals and terminal errors.
criteria.library: Build one generic consume over opaque sources with continue/stop handler decisions.
criteria.pull: Build shared opaque readers/writers with read_many, write_some, close and cancel plus recursive caller pumps.

surface.instructions: Which stream surface should the implementation build first?

criteria.distinct: Forbid repeated selectors; every scripted read needs its own lexical call site.
criteria.fifo: Allow repeated selectors on one read site; rows are consumed in order with argument verification.
criteria.single: Allow one row per site and reuse it for every visit; multi-read transcripts are out of scope.

transcript.instructions: How should multi-read fixture transcripts be spelled?

state: Nine complete Can programs compare three stream surfaces across three workflows: W1 reads a large file, decodes JSONL lines and stops after a typed id predicate; W2 drains interleaved child stdout/stderr into grouped progress state with a cancel budget and reaps the exit; W3 serves one socket session with text/binary/drain/close events and stops on handler failure. Surface L (shared library) drives every workflow through one generic stream::consume over opaque sources with handler decisions continue/stop. Surface D (per-domain) repeats that contract under files::/process::/socket::-owned names with per-domain terminal errors. Surface E (shared-event pull) exposes opaque readers/writers with read_many/write_some/close/cancel, empty batch as normal end, and caller-written recursive pumps with explicit closes. All nine programs parse with the current grammar; canlc assert rejects each only on its hypothetical catalogue entries (unknown package stream/socket, or no eligible type for the decision nominals). Verified precedents: array.fold already checks $callback handlers with derived errors; sql::with_transaction with sql::decision proves the decision-value shape; direct self-recursion executes with real-can evidence; withFixture selects rows by assertion name and consumes them FIFO across per-visit identities, so per-read transcripts detect overrun (missing fixture) and underrun (unused fixture); opaque givens are engine-supplied and referenced from when rows; error arms bind (as failed) and re-raise by reconstruction. Pinned Bun 1.4.2 probes observed: zero native pulls before getReader and two pulls after two reads; cancel settles a pending read as done with no value and releases the lock; chunk objects are distinct per read, slice() detaches a boundary copy, and streaming TextDecoder reassembles split UTF-8; FileSink.write reports accepted bytes but write-after-end is silent, so ended-state enforcement is adapter-side; two child writes arrived as one four-byte chunk, so chunking is not message-aligned. Fixed constraints: no new grammar unless a surface justifies it; catalogue additions only; lifecycle open to closing to closed with exactly one terminal publication and cleanup that preserves the primary failure; no scheduler beside owner.ts. Measured costs: E needs a close per terminal arm (W3 pull is 152 lines with echo writes versus 81-88 for callback styles); L hides loop, cancellation coupling and cleanup inside the adapter; D repeats one contract three times and strands its exit query without a handle (ambient exit_of()). Advice is advisory; acceptance evidence decides.
